verse.translation: The doer who is free from attachment, does not speak of himself, is full of steadiness and enthusiasm, and unmoved by success or failure, is called sattvic.

verse.line: Effort brings results, sooner or later, depending on time and place. That timing is what we call fate.

prasang.title: Vasishtha on self-effort: fate is only your past effort
prasang.summary: Vasishtha's first teaching to Rama is a long case for self-effort. What people call fate is simply the fruit of their own past effort, and present effort can overcome it, as the stronger of two rams wins. He also says not to torment yourself over what was beyond your power, and to steer your habits gently, like raising a child.
prasang.lesson: Your past effort shaped today; today's effort shapes tomorrow. Don't grieve what was never in your hands.

verse.meaning: Vasishtha tells the young Rama that what people call fate is simply the fruit of their own past effort arriving early or late. The timing is not the point. What matters is that your present effort shapes what comes next. He says not to torment yourself over what was never in your hands, and to steer your habits gently, like raising a child. The verse asks you to see that your resolve is the only thing that truly builds your life.
verse.for_you: You signed your first customer. The next ten months will test whether your footing comes from the contract or from your own resolve. Let the praise or the silence of the next few weeks come and go. Keep steering your habits gently, and let the work itself decide what comes next.

verse.speaker: Bhartrihari
verse.sanskrit: निन्दन्तु नीतिनिपुणा यदि वा स्तुवन्तु लक्ष्मीः समाविशतु गच्छतु वा यथेष्टम् । अद्यैव वा मरणमस्तु युगान्तरे वा न्याय्यात्पथः प्रविचलन्ति पदं न धीराः ॥
verse.line: Let them praise or blame, let money come or go: the steady don't step off the right path.
verse.translation: Let the worldly-wise blame or praise; let fortune come or go as she pleases; let death come today or ages hence: the steadfast do not move a step from the path of what is right.
verse.why: Setbacks rarely last for those who keep going on the right path.

prasang.title: Nitishatakam: On steadfastness
prasang.summary: Steadfastness: the gods kept churning the ocean past jewels and poison until they found nectar; the steady do not leave the right path whatever people say. A struck ball bounces back and a cut tree grows again.
prasang.lesson: Setbacks rarely last for those who keep going on the right path.

verse.meaning: Bhartrihari writes that the steadfast do not move a step from the path of what is right. He lists the noise of the world, the coming and going of money, and even the certainty of death. None of it makes them step off. Setbacks rarely last for those who keep going. The verse asks you to hold the right path steady even when the world around you is pulling in every direction.
verse.for_you: Your phone will ring with praise and with doubt. Let the money come and go as it does. Keep your hand on the work that is yours to build. The path you chose is the only one that leads to the next ten customers.

weeks.title: The first customer is not the finish line

script: You signed your first paying customer after months of work. The high is real, and you know the hard part begins now. You want to stay grounded through the year ahead without riding the highs and lows. You are choosing to be the person who builds the next ten.

Krishna is speaking to Arjuna on the battlefield. He is laying out the difference between a clear mind and a restless one. He describes the person who acts with steadiness. This person does not cling to results. They do not boast about what they are doing. They move forward with quiet resolve and enthusiasm. When success comes, they do not swell with pride. When failure comes, they do not collapse. Krishna said:
मुक्तसङ्गोऽनहंवादी धृत्युत्साहसमन्वितः, सिद्ध्यसिद्ध्योर्निर्विकारः कर्ता सात्त्विक उच्यते.
In plain words: Free of clinging and boasting, full of resolve and enthusiasm, unchanged by success or failure: the best kind of doer.

This is the best kind of doer. They act without attachment to the fruit. They do not speak of their own greatness. They carry steadiness and enthusiasm together. They are unmoved by success or failure. This is easier said than done, because every outcome will test your resolve.
When the next high or low arrives, let it pass through you. Do not let the first customer decide how you feel about the next one. Stay with your work.

depth.life: You have just signed your first paying customer after months of work. The high is real, but you are choosing to stay unchanged by the next high or low. That resolve is what will carry you through the year ahead.
depth.points: The best kind of doer is free from attachment and boasting. They are full of steadiness and enthusiasm, and they remain unchanged by success or failure. This means the joy of building is not found in the result, but in the resolve itself.
depth.practice: Write down one small action you will take tomorrow that is not tied to the outcome of your first customer.
depth.question: What does it mean to act with enthusiasm while staying free from the result?
